column2: No, Regions have none under them
No Unrest is ever tucked under a Region.
What is your default hand limit?
Five cards, unless an effect says otherwise.
Your Nation deck is empty and you shuffle your discard pile. What can you add?
A Development card, by paying its cost
A Market card
You choose a card from your Development area and pay its cost.
What does the Glory card do?
It gives 3 Regions
It makes you Abandon 3 Regions in play to gain a Fame card
It removes 3 Unrest
Three Regions in play go to the discard pile in exchange for a Fame card.
Is a card Reserved under a Region "in play"?
No, but it counts for scoring
It is no longer in your play area: no ability, no discard possible, but its points count.
Do cards left in your Nation deck at the end count for scoring?
Neither the Nation deck nor the Development area count.
When does the Solstice happen?
At the start of each turn
At the end of each round, once everyone has played
Once per game
It is the very last step of each round.
How much is a Progress token in your reserve worth at the Countdown?
0 points
1 point
2 points
1 point per Progress in reserve. Those placed on cards don't count.
Your personal draw pile, face down. You draw your hand from it. Empty when you need to draw: you shuffle your discard pile.
5 cards by default. Gained cards almost always arrive here.
Face up. Played and discarded cards go here, as well as Abandoned Regions.
Play area
Your permanent cards, especially your Regions. They stay here until an effect removes them.
Your nation's cards, face down, placed crosswise on the Accession. One card comes out each time you shuffle your discard pile.
Last card of the Nation deck. When it joins your discard pile, your State card flips: Barbarian becomes Empire.
Face-up cards you add one by one, paying their cost, once the Nation deck is empty. Developing the last one triggers the Countdown.
State card
Barbarian or Empire. It holds your available Action and Exhaust tokens and determines which cards you can play from your hand.
Power card
Your nation's own power. It can often be Exhausted like a card in play.
The cards put into History under your Power card. Out of play, but their points count.
Reserve
Your available Materials, Population and Progress tokens. Start: 3 Materials, 2 Population, 1 Progress.
Reserved cards
Cards slid under a card in play. Unusable, but counted for scoring.
Header icon
Marks a permanent card, which stays in play once placed, or an Attack, which hits the other players.
The card's title. Some cards refer to each other by name.
Its colour matches the category. It is used to sort the cards during setup. Cards with no category have a grey banner.
State icon
Barbarian or Empire. You only play the card from your hand if your State card matches.
Type icons
City, River, Ocean, Fertile land, etc. No effect of their own, but other cards refer to them.
What the card does and when. Keywords stand out.
Development cost
On Development cards: what you pay to add it to your deck.
Nation colour
Coloured bottom-left corner: the card belongs to a nation. No colour: common card.
Starting location
Icon telling where the card goes at setup: in play, Nation deck, Accession, Development or Unrest pile. No icon: starting deck.
Player count limit
A card marked 3+ isn't used with two players or solo; a card marked 4 is only used with four.
Number
The card's reference. The first digit gives the box: 1 for Classics.
Category
Region, Tradition, Civilised, Tributary, Fame or Unrest. Determines what you can Acquire or Innovate.
Victory points
Fixed, conditional, variable (10 at most) or negative value.
Choose a nation and take all its cards (look at the colour of the bottom-left corner).
Place your Power card in front of you. If it has two sides, use side B to start.
Place your State card Barbarian side up.
Place 3 Action tokens and 5 Exhaust tokens on your State card.
Line up your Development cards face up: this is your Development area.
Place your Accession card face up. Shuffle your Nation cards and place them on top, face down, crosswise.
Take 3 Materials, 2 Population and 1 Progress: this is your reserve.
Set aside your nation's starting Unrest cards (Celts, Vikings): they will join the common pile. Remove the 3+ or 4 cards that don't match the player count.
Shuffle the remaining cards: this is your deck. Leave room on the right for your discard pile and play area.
Draw 5 cards.
Form the supply: all tokens within reach.
Sort the common cards by the colour of their banner.
Remove the common cards marked 4.
Remove the common cards marked 3+ and 4.
With four players, all common cards are used.
Place all the Unrest cards face up in a pile, with those set aside by the players. Leave room next to it for the Exile pile.
Place King of Kings side A up. Shuffle the other Fame cards and place on top of it, crosswise, a face-down pile of
cards. The surplus goes back in the box unseen.
Form three face-down decks of
cards each: Region, Tradition, Civilised.
Shuffle together all the Tributaries and the rest of the Regions, Traditions and Civilised cards: this is the Main deck, placed horizontally.
Flip one card from each of the Region, Tradition and Civilised decks, and two cards from the Main deck: the five Market cards.
Tuck an Unrest under each Market card that isn't a Region.
Place 1 Progress on each white-banner Market card (the Civilised cards).
Pick the first player at random. Place the Solstice token between them and the player on their right.
The order for almost all your turns.
You take Actions and use Exhaust abilities, in whatever order and combination you like.
You stop when you can't or don't want to do anything more.
Then Cleanup.

you have cards to play or useful Exhaust abilities.
One chosen card, without Unrest.
Put your whole hand into your discard pile.
Innovate a Region, a Tradition, a Civilised or a Tributary. Not a Fame card.
No Action, no Exhaust ability. Passive abilities stay active.

The big clean-up.
Return as many Unrest cards from your hand to the pile as you like, without paying anything.

Fast expansion: conquer Regions to play Glory and gain Fame. Your Legions extend conquests once you are an Empire. Bring the City of Rome into play and evolve it. A few extra cities help your deck cycle.

Subjugate the other nations: pile up Tributaries and expand your territories. Once an Empire, attack with the Battering Ram and spread Unrest with Persian Gold, or bet on Satrap to gain Actions, after securing your Materials with Windmills.
Macedonians
Rather peaceful

The expansion nation: pile up Regions and keep them in play. Conquer stays useful once you are an Empire thanks to Alexander and his Cavalry. Play Glory early and often, in synergy with the Phalanxes, and Reserve cards under your surplus Regions.
Control the Market and amass Materials with Caravans and Merchant Ships. Once an Empire: Elephants led by Hannibal, or Monopoly to send Unrest and unwanted cards to others. Look for oceans.
Special rule: at Cleanup, you add Materials onto a Market card instead of Progress. The amount depends on your Power card.

Aggressive play: acquire cards and hand out Unrest with your Druids. Without Prosperity, your resources come from Cattle Raid and Cerridwen's Cauldron. You aim to lengthen the game to Develop your five cards.
Special rule: the side A effect of your Power card hinders others, but it isn't an Attack: no protection against it.
Nomads: expand your territory and exploit your Regions with Tents and Mounted Archers. A light and very fast deck thanks to Tamga, but poor in points: watch for variable-points cards in the Market.

Cities and technology. Colonists and Greek Mercenaries launch your expansion. Once an Empire, Science helps you progress and the Olympic Games help you manage. Lighthouse manipulates the Exile pile: remember what you Exile.
Your Nation deck offers you free cards, in an order you don't control. Lean on Gothja, and Reserve cards with your Regions and Sagas to tame your deck.

Special rules: you never become an Empire, you have no Development area and no History (a card to put into History is Discarded). The card at the bottom of your Nation deck is your Zenith: when it joins your discard pile, the end of the game is triggered and your State card doesn't flip.
Put a Region in play into your discard pile. Resources on it return to your reserve; a card Reserved under it is discarded too. Some effects let you Abandon only a Reserved card.
Take a visible Market card of the stated category, with its resources and the Unrest under it. The Market is refilled at once.
Action (gain, spend)
Gain: take an Action token from the supply, even beyond three. Spend: remove the number of tokens required, otherwise the effect is impossible.
The card is played without an Action token. At most once per turn for the same card. Costs written on the card are still due.
Add a resource
Take the resource from the supply and place it in the stated area or on the stated card.
The effect hits all other players, as much as possible. Some cards let you ignore it.
Barbarian / Empire
The sides of your State card. A card marked with a State can only be played from your hand if you are in that State. "If you are Barbarian / Empire": the effect or option only exists in that State.
Cards in play
A permanent card stays in play until an effect removes it. Its resources then return to your reserve; an Exhaust token placed on it only returns at the end of the turn.
Resolve only one of the options separated by OR. A full sentence after the list applies in every case.
Consider
Treat one icon as another until the end of the turn. The original icon no longer counts meanwhile. The effect always ends before the Solstice or the Countdown.
Discard
Put the card into your discard pile.
Move a resource
Move the resource from its owner's reserve to the stated place. No conversion possible. Resources already placed on cards are not moved.
Develop

Pay the cost of a card in your Development area, your choice, and put it into your discard pile. Through a card effect, this is possible even if a marker is already on the area, and without placing one. The Vikings never Develop.
Give a card
Choose a card from your hand; an opponent takes it into their hand.
Replace a Market card with another one. Tokens stay in place, the Unrest is renewed (except Region), and the removed card goes where the other one came from.
During your Activation order, place an Exhaust token on the card to resolve its effect. Once per turn per card. Putting a card down doesn't trigger its Exhaust ability.
Send the card to the Exile pile. From the Market: the Unrest goes back to its pile, the card is replaced. Impossible if the card carries tokens.
Gaining resources from Regions
Ability that triggers when a Region in play with the stated icon is used to gain you that resource, by its own effect or another card's such as Prosperity.
The cards put into History under your Power card. Out of play, but counted for scoring. Only you may look at them. The Vikings have none.

Announce a category, then take either a visible Market card (without the Unrest, which goes back to the pile) or the top face-down card of the matching deck. Tributary or empty deck: search the Main deck; nothing found: 2 Progress.
Effect permanently active while the card is in play: during all orders, the Solstice and the Countdown.
Return the required tokens from your reserve to the supply. 1 Progress can replace 1 Population or 2 Materials. No other conversion.
Your Nation cards face down on the Accession. Whatever happens, the Accession stays at the very bottom and is never shuffled with them.
Take cards from your deck into your hand. Empty deck: shuffle your discard pile and continue. You always draw the top card of the pile.
Draw, if possible
Like Draw, but never shuffling the discard pile: empty deck, you stop.
Place on your deck
Place the card (from your hand, unless stated otherwise) face down on your deck.
Take a Region in play back into your hand, with the cards Reserved under it. The resources return to your reserve. If you replay it this turn, you can Exhaust it again with another token.
Recover
Take the stated card into your hand, or into the specified area. In a face-up area, you choose. Recovering an Unrest: from the common pile; the last one triggers the Collapse.
Secretly look at the stated cards, then put them back, in the order of your choice. In the Fame deck, ignore King of Kings; in the Nation deck, ignore the Accession, unless it is the only card.
Return a card
Put an Unrest back into the common pile. Playing it from your hand: an Action and its cost. Through another card's effect: no cost.
Return a token
Take back an Exhaust token placed on one of your cards and put it back on your State card. You can reuse it this turn.
Slide a card from your hand, face up, under the relevant card in play. It is no longer in play, but counts for scoring and shares the fate of the card holding it.
Remove a resource
Return the stated resource to the supply. No conversion.
Effect resolved automatically at the end of each round.
All players / all other players
The first includes you, the second doesn't.

Look for the card in your hand, then your discard pile, then your deck, then your Nation deck (except the Accession). Stop as soon as it is found and reveal it. Shuffle the deck or the Nation deck if you searched them.
Steal resources
Take the stated tokens from the targeted players' reserves, as much as possible, without conversion.
Fourth resource, tied to the Trade Routes expansion.
Haggle, Trade, Profit
Keywords from the Trade Routes expansion. Without the expansion, ignore any mention of Haggle.
Effect resolved after all your other Solstice effects. Found on Horizons cards.

You must Pay 4 Materials. Your reserve: 2 Materials, 3 Population, 1 Progress.
How do you pay this cost?
2 Materials and 2 Population
Population never replaces Materials. Only Progress converts.
2 Materials and 1 Progress
1 Progress is worth 2 Materials when you pay in Materials: that adds up.
I can't pay
Yes you can: your Progress covers the 2 missing Materials.
Your State card shows Barbarian. You have a card marked Empire in hand. In the Market, another Empire card tempts you.
What can you do this turn?
Play the Empire card from my hand
Impossible: a card marked Empire can only be played from your hand if your State card shows Empire.
Acquire the Market's Empire card for later
Acquiring or Innovating is allowed whatever your State. You'll play it after your Accession.
Neither
The State icon only limits playing the card from your hand, not obtaining it.
Final Countdown. One of your star cards says "1 VP per Region". You own 13 Regions.
How many points does this card earn you?
13 points
A variable-points card is capped.
10 points
The cap is 10 points per star card, Power card included.
The card does score points, just capped at 10.
You refill the Market. The card flipped into the right-hand slot is a Region.
Do you tuck an Unrest under it?
Yes, as under every card
Every Market card gets one, except Regions.
There is never an Unrest under a Region. That is what makes Regions low-risk to acquire.
You are setting up a solo game, so with the quantities of a 2-player game.
How many face-down Fame cards do you place on King of Kings?
With 2 players or solo: 6 Fame cards, and 6 cards in each of the Region, Tradition and Civilised decks.
8 is the quantity for 4 players.
The surplus goes back in the box unseen: you don't know which Fame cards are missing.
Two Unrest cards from your nation have no icon in the bottom-left corner.
Where do they go at setup?
In my starting deck
A card with no starting icon is part of the initial deck. Your nation therefore starts with some trouble.
In the common Unrest pile
Only Unrest cards carrying the pile icon go there.
In the box
Only cards marked 3+ or 4 are set aside when the player count doesn't match.
